title: The Last Letter: Radiograph
statement: Kite's spine buckled and a disc slipped. An archive that has a damaged object makes an image of it before deciding anything, so this is the radiograph: the cotton field has become dark film with a faint measuring grid, the seven bowed vertebrae show as pale negatives with their inner panels lighter still, and the slipped green piece on the field has come out the only colour in the plate, because what is foreign to a body always does. The crease shows as a thin bright line, the way a fold shows on film. Nothing has been moved or mended. Before a repair there is a record. The next hand can read the plate, or go back to the object.
process: I kept the parent's exact composition, the seven fragments on their bowed curve with their rotations, the slipped green fragment, the crease and the dust, and inverted the whole image into a radiograph: a near-black field with a measuring grid, pale translucent fragments with brighter cores, a bright crease, and the green piece kept in full colour. A frame of film-edge marks surrounds the plate.
